FACILITIES

Experimental Facilities

From self-built rotating platforms to wave channels at different scales, our facilities provide controlled environments for observing and understanding geophysical fluid processes.

01

Large Rotating Tank

The tank is 1.1m in diameter and 0.2m in height, equipped with a 220v power supply system and a wifi camera, and three 1kW 538nm red sheet lasers. It is mainly used for experimental simulation of large-scale atmospheric and oceanic motions.

View facility ↗
02

Long Wave Channel

The tank is 2.4m long, about 0.12m wide, and 0.5m high, with sloping terrain at the bottom. One end is equipped with a wave maker (a stepper motor drives a belt track, hanging on a pentagonal hollow plexiglass block). It can produce approximately harmonic waves. As the wave propagates along the slope, the water depth decreases and the amplitude increases until it breaks. A bottle cap can be placed on the water surface to observe Stokes drift: the transport effect of finite amplitude waves on substances. There are several inlet/outlet ports at the bottom to create stratification.

View facility ↗
03

Mini Wave Channel

The tank is modified from a stratified tank. It is 1.0m long, about 0.1m wide, and 0.6m high. It produces approximately harmonic waves through a wave maker.
